title: Landstar Earns Top Rankings from Transport Topics
summary: Landstar ranks among North America’s top logistics providers, earning the No. 25 spot on Transport Topics’ 2026 Top 100 Logistics Companies list and No. 8 among freight brokerage firms.
body_text: Landstar System, Inc. earned the No. 25 spot on Transport Topics’ 2026 Top 100 Logistics Companies list, which ranks North America’s largest providers by 2025 gross revenue. The annual list highlights industry leaders across the continent. Landstar also achieved a No. 8 ranking on the publication’s Top 100 Freight Brokerage Firms list, reflecting its standing in brokerage services. By leveraging this network, along with advanced technology and industry experience, the company delivers flexible and scalable transportation solutions.

title: How to Invest as a Digital Nomad: Building Wealth While You Wander
summary: Don't let wanderlust stop your wealth-building journey! Explore smart investment strategies for digital nomads to secure a financially free future.
body_text: Working remotely and traveling the world is the dream, but building wealth with a constantly changing address takes a plan. This guide explains how to invest as a digital nomad: the options, the tax and currency considerations, and practical steps to start, so your money grows wherever you are. Ontop is a global payments platform that lets remote workers get paid and hold their income in a global account they control, which is the first step before any investment plan: keep more of what you earn. Key takeaways Digital nomads need a proactive investing plan since they rarely have employer retirement plans. Low-maintenance options (index funds, ETFs, robo-advisors) fit a location-independent life. Automate contributions and diversify to ride out market swings. Tax and currency complexity are the biggest challenges; a specialist advisor helps. Getting paid efficiently, without losing income to fees, is the foundation of investing. Why invest as a digital nomad? Secure your future: a nest egg cushions income swings and funds retirement anywhere. Beat inflation: investing helps your money outpace rising prices. Compounding: starting early turns small, regular investments into real wealth. Fund your freedom: financial independence sustains the nomadic lifestyle long term. Investment options for digital nomads Robo-advisors: automated, low-cost diversified portfolios based on your risk profile. Index funds and ETFs: a low-cost way to track a broad market or sector. Individual stocks: higher risk and potential return, needs research. Peer-to-peer lending: interest income, with default risk. Real estate crowdfunding: access to property deals with smaller minimums, but illiquid. Practical steps to start Open an investment account that accepts international investors. Set clear short-term and long-term goals. Automate transfers so you invest consistently. Diversify across asset classes to manage risk. Invest for the long term and stay tax compliant across the countries you earn in. Challenges to plan for Tax complexity: income from several countries needs expert guidance. Currency fluctuations: exchange-rate swings affect returns; holding income in a stable currency helps. Access: some options depend on your residency; global platforms widen the choice. Frequently asked questions How do digital nomads invest without an employer plan? They open their own brokerage or robo-advisor account, automate contributions, and build a diversified long-term portfolio. How do currency and fees affect nomad investing? Conversion fees and exchange swings quietly erode returns, so getting paid and holding income efficiently matters as much as the investments themselves. What is the easiest way to start? Automated index-fund or robo-advisor investing, funded by automatic transfers, is the lowest-maintenance starting point. Conclusion Investing as a digital nomad is a marathon: start early, automate, diversify, and stay compliant. It begins with keeping more of your income, then putting it to work while you explore the world.

title: Belden helps shape the future of quantum technologies by partnering with Quantum Security & Defence
summary: Partnering with Quantum Security & Defence, Belden will play a leading role in advancing practical pathways for quantum-safe networking and critical system resilience.
body_text: St. Louis, Missouri – Dec. 9, 2025 – Belden Inc. (NYSE: BDC), a leading global provider of complete connection solutions, is proud to strengthen its commitment to advancing secure connectivity in the quantum-AI era by partnering with Quantum Security & Defence (QSECDEF), the global orchestrator of the quantum-secure supply chain. From manufacturing to healthcare, the challenges organizations are facing have become so complex, data-intensive and interconnected that they can no longer be addressed with traditional computing alone. This is accelerating the move toward quantum approaches to solve high-stakes, computationally intensive problems. To support the transition, QSECDEF unites quantum professionals, leaders, academics and engineers from around the world to develop procurement standards, certification frameworks and education initiatives. The organization’s mission is to prepare enterprises and their leaders for a smooth, secure transition into quantum networking. With its experienced team of network infrastructure and cybersecurity experts, Belden stands ready to help QSECDEF advance practical pathways for quantum-safe networking and critical system resilience. Belden’s trusted, resilient and futureproof network infrastructure solutions will be essential to support quantum technologies as they move from the research stage to real-world deployment at scale. “Belden’s reputation for engineering excellence and leadership in secure connectivity make it a natural fit for our mission,” says Quantum Security & Defence CEO Anna Beata Kalisz Hedegaard. “Together, we aim to accelerate the adoption of quantum-secure standards and empower enterprises to prepare for the next generation of quantum secure communications and network security.” Recent work with the Chicago Quantum Exchange is just one example of how Belden is collaborating with leading industry partners to establish a strong foundation for quantum‑safe networking. This collaboration with QSECDEF will allow Belden to continue to expand its impact and support enterprises and critical infrastructure operators globally. “Harnessing the benefits of quantum depends on secure, resilient networks that enterprises can trust,” says Belden Vice President, Emerging Technologies Vijay K. Vallala. “We partnered with QSECDEF because of its unique focus on creating the frameworks that can be used to build quantum roadmaps. Together, we can help bring quantum-secure networking to operational environments." About Belden Belden Inc. delivers complete connection solutions that unlock untold possibilities for our customers, their customers and the world. We advance ideas and technologies that enable a safer, smarter and more prosperous future. Throughout our 120+ year history we have evolved as a company, but our purpose remains – making connections. By connecting people, information and ideas, we make it possible. We are headquartered in St. Louis and have manufacturing capabilities in North America, Europe, Asia and Africa. For more information, visit us at www.belden.com ; follow us on Facebook , LinkedIn and X/Twitter . body_text: View All News Rambam Health Care Campus, EOS and PTC Partner to Establish Advanced In-House Digital Implant Engineering Center July 15, 2026 HAIFA, Israel and KRAILLING, Germany and BOSTON , July 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rambam Health Care Campus , EOS , and PTC today announced collaboration to establish a Digital Implant Engineering Center at Rambam in Haifa, Israel. A dedicated team of engineers and physicians plan to work together to design, develop, and produce customized patient implants and devices using metal 3D printing. The collaboration leverages Rambam's clinical expertise, EOS's industrial 3D printing technology, and PTC's advanced Creo® computer-aided design (CAD) solution. The initiative aims to enhance personalized care and improve patient outcomes by integrating advanced 3D-CAD design, validation, manufacturing, and quality within a unified framework. Patient-specific implants have been shown to provide better anatomical fit and surgical accuracy. Producing implants at point of care improves collaboration between surgeons and developers, reduces reliance on external suppliers and speeds up patient treatment. This approach also shortens procedures and recovery times, helps maintain high quality standards, and helps meet regulatory requirements for safety and effectiveness. "Personalized care represents the future of medicine, and Rambam is establishing a significant benchmark with its dedicated in-house center," said Dr. Michal Mekel, Director General (CEO), Rambam Health Care Campus. "This initiative supports Rambam in developing patient-specific care that emphasizes innovation, clinical value, and operational excellence." "Point-of-care innovation in healthcare depends on integrating advanced industrial-grade additive manufacturing with validated hospital workflows. Our open software structure enables such scan-to-print workflows," said Nikolai Zaepernick, CSO, EOS. "We view this as a vital step toward a repeatable, highly responsive and digitally connected model for patient-specific care." "Cutting-edge personalized implants require a connected digital foundation that ties together clinical need, design, manufacturability and workflow discipline," said Dr. Ronen Ben-Horin, Vice President Technology, PTC. "The Digital Engineering Center at Rambam demonstrates how intelligent digital engineering drives innovation. We see this development as a breakthrough for the health care industry and are proud our technology will play a central role." This initiative represents a significant move toward digitally integrated, clinically driven solutions for complex, customized treatments. By combining clinical expertise, engineering knowledge, structured processes, and advanced additive manufacturing, the partners aim to create a system that enables patient-specific innovation. This framework could help major hospitals around the world access tailored implant solutions, leading to faster and better patient care. About Rambam Health Campus: Rambam is a 1,100-bed academic hospital serving over 2.7 million residents of northern Israel. Rambam provides comprehensive medical services in all medical specialties and is a tertiary referral center for 12 district hospitals. The hospital provides the full spectrum of patient care, as well as engaging in clinical research. As northern Israel's only tertiary medical center, Rambam is the country's most experienced trauma facility, with extensive experience treating severe injuries, and is home to one of Israel's largest pediatric and adult oncology centers, where the use of implants is increasingly common. Rambam Health Campus was recently ranked as one of the most recommended hospitals in Israel. In addition to serving the residents of northern Israel, Rambam serves the IDF Northern Command, UN peacekeeping forces, and the U.S. Sixth Fleet. Many of Rambam's physicians are internationally recognized for their clinical expertise. Physicians participate in innovative research projects to bring new treatments not only to their patients, but to the wider global community. About EOS : EOS provides responsible manufacturing solutions via industrial 3D printing technologies to organizations around the world. Since 1989, EOS has shaped the future of manufacturing by enabling its customers to innovate and differentiate through expert guidance, technology and services, leveraging its end-to-end additive manufacturing (AM) industry partnerships. From strategy to education to production, EOS is the leading global partner for both metal and polymer AM solutions, accelerating time-to-market for its customers through high-quality production efficiencies and sustainable solutions. About PTC: PTC (NASDAQ: PTC) is a global software company that enables industrial and manufacturing companies to digitally transform how they engineer, manufacture, and service the physical products that the world relies on. Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, PTC employs over 7,000 people and supports more than 30,000 customers globally. For more information, please visit www.ptc.com .
